scope: Focused actual owner-integration journeys; broad CI remains required

images.alt: Emma Smith at twenty three, wearing a long blue dress, rides sidesaddle at a gallop on a brown horse up a leaf covered slope in autumn, leaning forward with both hands on the reins and her eyes on the path ahead.
Emma Smith at thirty one, wearing a brown dress, stands by a window holding a small bound book in both hands and looking down at it.
Emma Smith at thirty four, wearing a gray dress, sits by a window with her hands folded in her lap and her gaze lowered.
Emma Smith at thirty eight, wearing a dark green dress, stands in the open doorway of her home with one hand resting on the door.
Emma Smith at seventy four, wearing a dark gray dress, sits speaking, one hand raised in conversation, her gaze toward the one she is speaking with.

image.alt: Jesus prays outdoors beneath the night sky.

context.heading: Scripture reflection: A night in prayer

previousSibling.text: Family tradition, recorded in Church History Topics, tells that Emma’s father overheard young Emma praying in the woods and was moved by what he heard.

image.alt: Jesus and His disciples sing together.

previousSibling.text: Sources for this part of Emma’s story Emma Hale Smith, Church History Topics Collection of Sacred Hymns for the Church of the Latter Day Saints, Joseph Smith Papers Doctrine and Covenants 25:11-12

image.alt: Jesus speaks to a disciple as others gather remaining bread.

context.heading: Scripture reflection: Let nothing be lost

previousSibling.text: Sources for this part of Emma’s story Female Relief Society of Nauvoo, Church History Topics Nauvoo Relief Society Minute Book, in The First Fifty Years of Relief Society, Church Historians Press Emma Hale Smith, Church History Topics

image.alt: Jesus departs by boat on the water.

previousSibling.text: On June 27, 1844, Joseph and his brother Hyrum were killed at Carthage. Emma was thirty-nine and pregnant. Her responsibilities now included mourning her husband and preparing to raise the child who would be born after his death.
